feedback.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0,1]\times [1,2]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}y-5y+8 \\ x{y}^{2}-3\end{aligned}].
$$

Fill in the blanks in the matrix equation below that defines the first iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting at the point $[1,\,1]^{T}.$

| $[$ | $3$ | $-4$ | $]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})\,=[$ | {{field-1}} | $].$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-2}} | {{field-3}} | $2$ |  |  |  |
feedback.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be re-written as

$$
{J}_{f}({x}_{n})({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-f({x}_{n}).
$$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}y-5y+8) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}y-5y+8) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}(x{y}^{2}-3) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(x{y}^{2}-3)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}y & {x}^{3}-5 \\ {y}^{2} & 2xy\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}y & {x}^{3}-5 \\ {y}^{2} & 2xy\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}y-5y+8 \\ x{y}^{2}-3\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}y & {x}^{3}-5 \\ {y}^{2} & 2xy\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}y-5y+8 \\ x{y}^{2}-3\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}3(1)^{2}(1) & (1)^{3}-5 \\ (1)^{2} & 2(1)(1)\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}(1)^{3}(1)-5(1)+8 \\ (1)(1)^{2}-3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
